responsibilities: Build and own scalable data pipelines, transformations, analytical datasets, and reusable data products using SQL and Python.
Analyze B2C, product, and customer data to identify trends, performance drivers, and actionable insights.
Translate business and product questions into reliable metrics and decision-support solutions that help teams measure performance and understand customer behavior.
Design, build, and deploy LLM-powered applications, agents, and analytics workflows using RAG, tool calling, MCP, and modern agent frameworks.
Develop reusable AI tools that enable analysts and business users to interact with data, automate analysis, and generate insights.
Evaluate, monitor, and continuously improve AI solutions in production, focusing on accuracy, reliability, cost, and safety.
Integrate data platforms, analytics systems, APIs, and AI components into reliable, secure, and maintainable services.
Contribute to the architecture and design of scalable data and AI systems in collaboration with platform and engineering teams.

A governed metrics layer — reliable, reusable definitions for retention, conversion, LTV and other core B2C metrics, built on BigQuery / Fabric with governed definitions in OpenMetadata, that every team and every AI tool draws from.
An analytics copilot — a natural-language interface that lets product managers and business users ask questions of the data and get trustworthy, sourced answers.
Automated analysis workflows — agents that handle recurring analyses (weekly performance reviews, anomaly triage, funnel diagnostics) and surface what matters.

Reusable AI tooling — skills, knowledge sources, documentation, MCP servers, and ready-to-use scripts that AI tools can call for data extraction, analysis, and visualization, so building the next AI feature is fast and safe.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: A governed metrics layer — reliable, reusable definitions...focusing on accuracy, reliability, cost, and safety
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: "Bias to action" and "Build, ship, learn fast" sit in the company values, but the role's own bullets keep returning to "reliable", "governed" and "accuracy", more than twice as often, so rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: Pearl is AI for professional services at global scale
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: B2C metrics and analytics copilots for a professional-services marketplace carry no regulatory or financial-reporting language, so moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity: built on BigQuery / Fabric with governed definitions in OpenMetadata
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A named warehouse and catalogue plus separate "platform and engineering teams" show an existing, growing data function, so mid.
evidence.jd_authorship: agents that handle recurring analyses (weekly performance reviews, anomaly triage, funnel diagnostics)
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Bullets name concrete builds, methods (RAG, MCP, tool calling) and tools (BigQuery, Fabric, OpenMetadata), so hiring_manager.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: You'll work directly with product, growth, and business teams on real B2C and customer data.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The main audience is product and growth teams and product managers using B2C retention, conversion and funnel metrics, so product.
evidence.autonomy_level: Build and own scalable data pipelines...Contribute to the architecture and design
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role owns pipelines and metrics but only "contributes to" architecture alongside platform teams, so mixed.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate builds the metrics layer, MCP servers and copilots that AI tools draw from, so ai_enabler.
evidence.testing_framing: Evaluate, monitor, and continuously improve AI solutions in production, focusing on accuracy, reliability, cost, and safety.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Evaluating and monitoring the accuracy of production solutions is a responsibility the role owns, so responsibility.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Trust in answers matters but the posting is framed around building and delivery, so moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The listed outputs are new systems (a metrics layer, an analytics copilot, agent workflows), so greenfield.
evidence.loss_aversion: "get trustworthy, sourced answers" Trustworthy AI answers as a product goal, secondary to building.
